about:
Plastic Mold Technology operates from Kentwood, Michigan. The company traces its roots to 1958 when Adrian Woldring founded Woldring and Associates as an electrical discharge machining (EDM) sales business. By the late 1960s the firm had shifted to building plastic injection molds, primarily for the automotive sector. After Woldring's retirement in 1974, Gary Proos took on joint ownership and acquired the company outright in 1984.

Today the shop provides prototype and production tooling for a broad spectrum of injection molding processes. Its capabilities include standard injection molding, insert molding, second-shot overmolding, glass encapsulation, stack molds, gas assist, two-shot molding, rotary molding, and reaction injection molding (RIM). The facility handles both prototype and high-volume production tooling, though specific facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not disclosed.

The company's customer base centers on the automotive industry, where it has supplied molds for decades. It also serves other sectors requiring complex multi-material or multi-component tooling, though no additional industries are named in its public materials.

Plastic Mold Technology emphasizes the deep experience of its management and shop-floor personnel as a key differentiator, positioning that institutional knowledge as the foundation for delivering complex tooling solutions.
